changes.before: If b is copied from a instead, why does the final output still read 2 7?
changes.after: Let a vector transfer its stored data, then give the source a known value.

before: std::move from <utility> does not itself move bytes or empty an object. It casts an expression so a receiving operation may use move semantics. Standard containers can transfer owned storage efficiently.

After moving this vector into b, b has the original values. The source vector remains valid but its value is unspecified; do not predict its size. Calling clear then push_back gives a a known new value.

a.clear() removes every element, leaving a.size() equal to zero; it returns no value. The later push_back then establishes the new element.
Moving is not reference aliasing. Reusing a after resetting it does not change b. Small scalar moves can just copy; std::move is not a universal speed switch.

Expected output or behavior: 2 7
. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Print b.size() after the move; do not assert a particular moved-from size. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: Moving lets an object hand owned resources to another object. std::move, from <utility>, marks a value so the receiving operation may move from it. std::move alone does not transfer anything; the receiving operation does the work.
After this vector move, b has the original items. a still exists and can be used, but do not rely on a particular set of remaining contents unless the operation promises one.
b and a are separate vectors. Changing a afterward does not change b. Moving a simple number may just copy it, so std::move is not a guarantee of faster code.
The program prints 2 7. b keeps the original first item, two. clear() removes any items left in a, and push_back puts seven into it.
clear() gives a a known empty state before the new item is added. The output therefore does not depend on guessing a's contents immediately after the move.

before.question: If b is copied from a instead, why does the final output still read 2 7?
choices: Copying is identical to moving internally
The later clear/push establishes a fresh a in either case
before.explanation: The final operations deliberately overwrite a’s contents, so the output does not reveal the different transfer/copy work.

after.question: Copy a into b instead of moving it. Why does the final output still read 2 7?
choices: Copying and moving always do identical work.
The later clear and push_back give a the same new contents either way.
Both vectors share their first item.
after.explanation: b receives the original values. The later operations replace a's contents, whether b was copied or moved.
